comments.text: This set is a big step up in what a material artist gets. Round 1 was strong on terrain, and this pass finally has wood, stone mosaic, cane, braid, fur, scales, marbling, agate, leaves and paint. The best work is either a recognisable material from one node (knot-flow, pinnate-venation, geode-field, advected-scatter, triaxial-weave) or a plumbing idea that multiplies every other node (cell-domain, seed-value, seed-route, cellular-multi, domain-tile). Figures such as flame, aurora and rain read at once through a ramp, though each is a one subject node. Motion ideas were judged from frames only. The weak zones are dots-on-black, of which there are far too many variations that differ only in a guarantee; terrain and level design utilities that give me nothing to look at; and technical coherent noises with no visible gain. Combed stroke and zebra families have too many near copies and should collapse into one node each. Costs on many of the best flow filters are bake only, which is fine for me but should be stated. Next in line after my 15 build_next picks: ink-drop-layers, geode-field, flame-licks, clumped-strands, conic-cells, lens-ridges, and spot ordering on StampScatter. What is still missing is the unglamorous half of a material graph: edge wear and cavity dirt masks from a height input, per tile directional gradients, a directional and non-uniform blur driven by a mask, and tiling shown by default; the sheets never show a tiling test, and a single float output means a multi-map PBR look must still be built by hand from sibling nodes.

Strong where it treats terrain as geology or control. The real gains are fractals that decide where detail goes (morse-lock, iso-focus, fractal-spectrum), crater hierarchies, jointed rock volumes, the first truly native sphere tools, cave structure, and gameplay constraints like pads and graded roads. Many of the abilities with dull images, such as quota, forecast, cdf and pinned, matter more to me than half the pretty pictures. A whole group is off target for this lens: weaves, Islamic tilings, kaleidoscopes, stripes, coats and most ornamental domain maps are good images I would never use on ground, and about a quarter of the set scores 2 or below from me. Costs are also a concern, since several terrain winners are 40x to 170x and so bake only, which is fine for a baked heightmap but not for a runtime planet. Motion ideas I mostly judged from stills and vols, opening frames only for boil-pot and seeing small frames on the sheet for aurora-curtains and glass-caustic. Still missing: continent-scale layout, meaning plate boundaries that raise mountain belts and control where coasts go; glacial valleys with U profiles and moraines; rivers that flow to the sea from any supplied height, since sphere-charts crossfades rivers at chart bands instead of connecting them and none of the drainage prototypes I saw drains an arbitrary height into connected rivers; a sphere-native fractal rather than charts; lakes that sit at the correct level on terrain; and a clear LOD contract across the set, since few ideas even raise the question, fractal-forecast and nested-fbm being the clear ones.

The set is richer and stranger than I expected from noise. Its best move is cross-breeding: voronoi-drum, jigsaw-gauge, advected-scatter and flow-shock-scales got their surprise by joining two things, and the second round beats the second pass on that account. Ideas like fibre-field, normal-lookup and closest-point-transport treat a field's geometry as a coordinate, which is the most fertile vein here. The figures group (web, leaves, flames, trees, galaxies) proves a pure function can draw objects. Those are spectacular but narrow, so ship a few and do not build a zoo. Honest dull spots: the dots-on-black group, most of the placement utilities, and the exact-statistics noises, all of which may be right but give an artist nothing to look at. The cellular family is oversubscribed, and many of its entries are one metric, gauge or output away from each other, so consolidate hard. Terrain work is competent but rarely surprises beyond the ErosionFilter baseline. Motion is thin: mostly loops and scrolls, with phase-morph, vortex-pair-billows and boil-pot as the few ideas with real events, and I judged all motion from frames only. Still missing: composition. Nearly everything is a statistically homogeneous texture, and only domain-mobius, the hyperbolic disc and a few others have a focal point or a structure across the frame. Also absent: glyphs and writing, architecture and urban layout, nodes that grow in visible generations, and asymmetry between scales. Next after my build list: FractalWindow (fractal-spectrum plus zoom-loop, since a wrapping Center is the endless zoom), PhaseOps (local-phase plus phase-morph, since demodulate is what morph wants), a hybrid direction on BurgersSteepen (flow-shock-scales, burgers-fold-strata), CrossBedding, and quasi-domain as a QuasiTile output. Seam data was mostly not scanned, so my notes make no claim of clean; voronoi-drum is the one non-ID output with jumps reported, and it should be checked before it is built.

What the set does well: it moves on from new kernels to new abilities. The best results are guarantees and interfaces that nobody ships: topology that fractal octaves cannot break, the exact expectation of unevaluated octaves, conditioning a noise through chosen values, stamps measured through a warp's inverse, strand diagrams that always alternate, and erosion on real 3D isosurfaces. Fixed-point warps and Newton charts turn out to be a rich seam, giving creased, folded and satin looks that forward warps cannot reach. Known tricks in new clothes, which I marked in the notes: LIC, Kuwahara, hg_sdf, sparse convolution, KIFS, mode 7, Heartfelt, Gerstner, Shepard zoom, the Z-sampler in quota-cells, geomorphons, spherical Fibonacci. Several of these are still worth having, because no noise library has them, but they are ports, not discoveries. The second-pass cellular group is the weakest in novelty and the most over-called; dull dot fields and combed fur are heavily over-produced, and the closed-form figures (galaxy, flame, drops, aurora) are demoscene pictures that do not compose. Still missing: a convincing cumulus (ico-billow fails), convincing open water (gerstner-sea is dull), and analytic footprint filtering, since super-sample is brute force and fractal-forecast is the only result pointing the right way. Just outside my build list, for lack of room: fold-print, adaptive-cellular, tropical-facet, pinnate-venation, coat-field, warp-strain, nested-foam, and hinge-tile as a TileDomain mode. Evidence notes: motion was judged for growing-cracks, vortex-pair-billows, aurora-curtains, domain-plume, flow-beads, phase-morph and zoom-loop, and for boil-pot; notes marked still only, plus flame-licks and glass-caustic, were judged from the sheet alone, so their motion is unverified. Rows that say not scanned were treated as no seam data, not as clean; only voronoi-drum (2274) and climate-diagram (8836, categorical by design) showed jumps among those scanned. Cost numbers were read as rough. Provenance claims are from my own memory of the literature and were not looked up.

The set is rich in looks and light on restraint. Stock plus lab is already 88 registered nodes, ids and pools are uint8 and capped at 255, and adding these 218 would pass that cap, so the first job is consolidation. Much of what earns a place needs no new node: a member, an enum entry or an output on a real node (Cellular, CellularLookup, CellularEdge, TubeNoise, Fade, Textile, TileDomain, StreakSmear, QuasiTile, ExchangeFoam). The best work here is the unglamorous group: domain-tile, seed-value, low-discrepancy-dither, exact-gaussian-noise, hard-core-cellular, morse-lock-fbm. They give guarantees and control rather than a new picture. The figures family looks wonderful and I would not ship any of it as a node; they could live as example graphs or a separate content pack. Duplication is heavy in four places: spots on black, combed grain, zebra stripes, drainage. Range is often held by a measured gain and a clamp, and many nodes are mostly background with a mean near -0.9, which is legal but surprising for users of Output Min and Max; every Output enum should state its range. The prototypers' artifact notes are candid and cost several of my favourites points: cdf-remap's stale calibration, domain-tile's Flatten overshoot, contrast-fade's unbounded range, jitter caps on hex lattice, poly-gauge and fibonacci-cells. Those belong in node docs. I read the artifact notes for about forty ideas, not all of them, so scores elsewhere rest on the images, the pack and each node's listed members and range. Cost figures here are scalar and rough, and many rows are not scanned yet, so I treated those as no data and only cited scan results where they exist. What is still missing: a shared Direction input convention (angle source, gradient of source, curl, half charge) so SteerablePerlin, PhasorNoise, StreakSmear, TubeNoise and FlowShingle do not each invent one; a shared gradient provider simpler than GenJet's per-node virtual; measured 4D for much of the second pass group, whose harness had no 4D path, because a missing or fallback 4D breaks GenTileable2D; a common Output naming vocabulary; and any proposal to retire or fold real nodes. Nothing in the set removes a node. build_next is capped at 15, so seed-route as a hybrid on SeedOffset, multiplicative-cascade, domain-kaleidoscope into ChiralWallpaper, cellular-circle-packing, foam-walls on ExchangeFoam, blend-mode and truchet-flow are the next wave.

Budget I scored against, using the handbook's 1.1 ns AVX2 Perlin as a rough scale: 10x is about 0.4 ms per 32^3 chunk and 80x about 3 ms, so a density node should stay near 25x, while a heightfield has 1/32 of the samples and can take about 100x. Pack costs are scalar and mostly 2D, so I used the 3D figures from result.json for key ideas and treat the rest as rough. 'Not scanned' I read as no data; only ideas showing a count have one, and that count is 2D only, so no 3D seam is cleared by it. Motion scores used the image for boil-pot, phase-morph, zoom-loop, flow-beads, domain-plume, and the sheet thumbnails for the rest. What the set does well: rock (joint-blocks, corestone, slab-field, poly-gauge), tube caves, placement guarantees (hard-core-cellular, quota-cells), and exact fractions (cdf-remap, exact-gaussian-noise, climate-diagram). Several promising ideas beat most keepers here: aquifer-field, dripstone, thin-cut, steered-tube, level-dendrite, strath-valley. Much of the set does not serve my use: stripes, fur, weaves, mandalas and figure stamps are many near copies of a few looks, attractive in 2D and shredded or empty in vol, and many are textures that belong in a bake or a shader. Still missing: a batch level bound or skip so sparse features do not pay full price in deep rock and open sky, since every 3D decorator here pays its worst case on every voxel. Measured 3D SIMD costs. Measured cave connectivity, which walkable-worms does not have. An ore vein node designed for that job, since fibre-field and warp-strain only approach it. LOD for anything beyond fractals, such as stamps, cells and tubes that alias or vanish at coarse sampling.

names: CellularEdge: Gauge and Strut outputs, Bend hybrid

items.why: One bisector pass gives a cell coordinate of 0 at the site and 1 on every wall. Facets, Chladni modes, thunderegg bands, strapwork and bent walls are output modes on it; a square layout keeps ModalCells' 1x price. Check the drum jumps first.

Once a cell has a coordinate that is 0 at the site and 1 on every wall, with per-wall hashes, facets, jigsaw walls, star strapwork and drum figures become output modes. Voronoi drum must lose its 2274 jumps first.

One search gives F1, edge distance, wall gauge, ID, per wall width and wobble as channels read by sibling nodes. Replaces a stack of costly CellularDistance nodes and gives stone, hide and jigsaw from one graph.

items.node: CellularEdge: Gauge and Strut outputs, Bend hybrid
items.why: All work from the same walls and bisectors as CellularEdge, so they should be outputs rather than nodes: a 0 to 1 gauge, connected struts at iso 0, and jigsaw walls. Cap jitter near 0.8 for the gauge: its brute force check still finds rare steps up to 0.057 in 2D there, and none above 1e-3 in 3D. Leave voronoi-drum's NodalLines out until its jumps are fixed.

names: FractalSpectrum: per-octave weight rule on one node
GenJet interface, with JetFractal as first user

items.why: All of these are one octave loop deciding where detail is allowed: by topology, by level, by spectrum, by slope. Add GenJet behind it so slope gates skip finite differences. This is the biggest visual jump over stock FBm in the set.

All of these set per-octave amplitude from a rule: gradient lock, level focus, winner take all, equaliser. One fractal with a rule enum and hybrids, not five nodes. Morse lock is the reason to build it.

items.node: FractalSpectrum: per-octave weight rule on one node
items.why: All of these are FBm with a per-point octave weight, so they should share a loop, normalisation and member set. Measured range is -0.97 to 0.96 or tighter in all five, and Lock at 0 is classic FBm. Drop the Odd and Cantor patterns as its notes advise. Morse's Max Slope needs a value for each real source, and every octave is paid for even at near zero weight.

All are per-octave weights at FBm cost: gated by slope, by level, or by a hybrid centre and width. One node, one octave loop, a mode enum. Morse lock would make a better default terrain than FractalFBm, and the spectrum mode gives per biome roughness.

items.node: GenJet interface, with JetFractal as first user
items.why: Gradient taps are the largest repeating cost across this set, in normals, slope masks and steering. Forward mode with finite difference fallback pays back across the whole library. It is a large interface change, so do it early or not at all.

Analytic doublets, vortices and dipoles on scattered sites, exposed both as a warp and as a stream function. Timber, bullseye checkers, paisley and ink mushrooms from one family at low cost, billows being the costly mode.
Closed-form doublet and dipole flows, exposed as a scalar, a warp, or a carried blob. Wood grain at 4.5x and mushroom billows are the same mathematics; billows need a cost pass from 45x.
Wood with knots at 4.5x, and the same field as a warp so planks, Textile or strata can run around obstacles. The wood problem solved in one family.

An exact expected value of the unevaluated octaves, plus coarse vertices that stay exact as octaves are added. Together they give planet LOD with masks and sea level that do not pop. They look like nothing, and they are the reason to use noise at planet scale.

LOD is where voxel worlds lose the most time. Distant chunks evaluate few octaves, keep the right coverage and sea level, and First and Max Octave members let coarse meshes agree with fine ones. Stock FractalFBm has none of these members today.
An exact expectation of octaves not evaluated gives LOD, masks and sea level that agree with the full fractal. This is the nearest thing in the set to analytic level of detail.

names: CdfRemap, Gaussian and Range inputs only

items.why: Monotone height remaps in one modifier: target a histogram for flat seabed and sharp coast, or question-mark terraces with unequal ledges. Cheap, works on anything, used on every terrain.
Histogram Scan and Histogram Range with a target shape. I need to set coverage and contrast before anything else in a material, and Remap cannot do it from an unknown distribution.

items.node: CdfRemap, Gaussian and Range inputs only
items.why: Shape the histogram and know roughly what comes out. Leave out the Measured input: its table is calibrated off the Gen path and goes stale when a child changes, which its author calls an unsolved API question, and a node must not sample a graph from a setter. Its notes give no coverage figures without calibration, so test that first. Compare against a SplineRemap preset, as 8 knots softened the coast and SplineRemap stops at 8.

Exact non overlapping circles and flow aligned ellipses, with a Z-buffered heap output for boulders over cobbles. A pebble floor is one of the most requested height maps, and overlap is the usual flaw.
Exact non-overlap across a wide size range, and the affine frame adds aspect and flow. Stamps need only one Source evaluation, so it is a cheap base for scatter too.
Exact non-overlap in closed form with a wide size range, with discs as the isotropic case of the per-triangle affine frame. Nothing stock can guarantee this.

A hash derived rank per cell is one kernel, and thresholding it gives spacing guarantees, exact quotas, coverage thinning, dither and macro shapes. Replaces hand written placement passes, and costs close to a plain cell hash. Note the port pays for all window cells.

Whole spots placed with guaranteed spacing, exact quota per region, and density read at the site. These prototypes differ only in how a candidate is accepted, so one Accept enum covers them. It is the mask that foliage and rocks actually need.

Six prototypes that all read as dots on black at thumbnail size. One node with Rank Below for the spacing guarantee, a Coverage hybrid with an Order enum, and a Rank output for quotas. It starts from the cheapest of them, and 4D works on an oblique plane. Quotas hold only in aligned blocks with constant Lo and Hi, so say so.

Uniform -1 to 1, about Perlin's cost, and a known good recipe. It belongs on White as an option, and the threshold can stay a graph. Document it as a mask source: the FFT is a regular lattice, not blue noise.
Per tile variety from a field, and a seed readable as a number that can drive rotation, tone or bevel. Small to build, and it makes every stamp and tile node look like real, varied material.
Treats the seed as a signal. Every parent that already reseeds per tile, stamp or grain gains per-object parameters at once, the largest breeding multiplier for the smallest code.

A small leaf that gives reseeding parents such as TileDomain and StampScatter real per-tile variation without new members on each. Ship Uniform, and add other outputs only on request; Decode needs a parent convention that does not exist.

Each resolves to (along, across, layer) for a Source, under a Path enum of Truchet, Hilbert, braid, triaxial or multigrid. Over-under stays consistent and any noise becomes grain along strands. Complements Textile.
Each is a set of strands with a provably consistent over-under rule. A layout enum (arbitrary curves, Truchet, braid word, triaxial, multigrid) over one strand profile, with Textile left as it is.
Basket kagome and braid as Textile Structure values, plus a knot mode. Same over-under logic and fibre streaks, cheap at 3 to 4x, and they read instantly.

names: TubeNoise: Floor, Direction and Bedding members
TubeNoise, with Floor, Bedding Planes and Steering members

items.node: TubeNoise: Floor, Direction and Bedding members
items.why: Small changes to a real node, all under 3.5x Perlin in the prototypes, and caves are what TubeNoise is for. Flat floors and bedding planes add control without a second tunnel node. All three still show flakes or shreds in places, so test them together.

items.node: TubeNoise, with Floor, Bedding Planes and Steering members
items.why: The best value per ns in the set: all under 5x, all on the existing offset vector. Flat floors, cave levels and directed tunnels together make caves a player can walk through. The real TubeNoise has no Floor member yet, so the walkable-worms merge has not landed. Measure connectivity before shipping.
Two small additions to an existing node at about 2x to 3x cost. Together they give cave levels with structure and floors a player can walk on.

Local corrections at known sites, without losing the terrain's character: level pads, graded roads with constant batter, exact heights at chosen points. No pointwise tool for this exists, and every game with a road needs it.

Cut and fill at a constant batter, for pads and roads, from the same kernel. Heightfield budget is fine at 15x to 33x because columns are far fewer than voxels. Skip route taps per batch when no lane is in reach.
Conditioning, known from geostatistics, is absent from graphics noise nodes. Passing through chosen values while keeping the source's texture is what a Fade dome cannot do.
Tiles and stones that follow a warp at constant grout and hold their size. Andamento mosaic, curved brick and leaded glass. No stock graph can get this, because a warp stretches the grout.
Stamps arranged by a warp but measured through its inverse Jacobian: mortar stays even while courses bend. Unlocks mosaic, cobbles and crowded pebbles from any existing warp.
Biome selection in climate space with solved weights, so the art lead can ask for 40 percent grassland and get it. Curved enclaves without a Voronoi look.
Biome selection by climate space with solved weights, so a requested share is what you get. This is a production need today and every team writes it by hand. Jumps are ID edges by design.
Overlay, Soft Light and friends in a single node, with a normalise option. Dull thumbnails, but every material graph is mostly blends, and a Multiply in [-1,1] flattens contrast.

Fixes the grey band in a crossfade with one option and a Correlation float, for about one InvSqrt. The smallest change on this list. Range is not analytically bounded and means drift between unlike sources, so leave it off by default and document the fitted gain.

Evaluates any child in its owning cell or shard's frame with the jump hidden under grout. It is flood fill plus transform, the core of nearly every tiled, cracked or terrazzo material. Shard plates and the cheap window are options on it.

The Voronoi partner to TileDomain: evaluate a child in its cell's frame with a per-lane seed, jump hidden under grout. Scan shows 0, one source eval per lane. Overlaps CellFrame, so settle how the two differ before adding it. The C0 promise covers only cell boundaries; a source's own jump passes through.

names: CellGauge, with a Site Layout enum

items.node: CellGauge, with a Site Layout enum
items.why: A cellular node with a flat faced gauge output and a choice of sites: cube, hex or BCC, wandering columns. Chiselled rock at 2x, basalt and bent columns, cut stone at grid friendly slopes. All are cheap and read well in 3D.

No new node. Honeycomb and even cells from one enum, cheaper in 3D and 4D, measured in all dims. Non Euclidean metrics are untested, so restrict the enum pairing or test it, and document the jitter caps its bound check found.
Any subgraph tiles at any period, warps and fractals included. Material artists ship tiling maps first and everything else second.

Any subgraph tiles at any period, including warps, which per-node Period members cannot do. Few members, 4D exists. Keep PeriodMember as the first choice for lattice sources, document the ghosting in the band and the 2^D source calls, and default Flatten off: it holds variance but took warped crackle to -1.57..1.48.
All three read a Source at a coordinate derived from a guide's local geometry: its normal, its contour foot point, its depth. One Chart enum gives chrome, satin petals and rinds.
A fixed gradient or Newton step yields foot point, depth and normal; the Source is read in that chart. Output modes give petal fans, even rinds and matcap metal from a single kernel.
Fixed loops of folds with an orbit output. KIFS is known from the demoscene, but trees with filleted crotches and exact 60 degree dendrites are new, and all three share one loop.
Figures grown by folding space, with 2D and solid 3D forms. Trees, roots, coral and snow crystals are the most surprising output in the whole set, and it needs only about 7x Perlin.
Nothing else gives dented older rings and true deposit order. Add a Source per drop and it becomes agate, marbled terrain and tissue from one kernel.
A closed-form deposit stack with true ordering: later drops dent earlier ones. No warp or blend reproduces this, and it gives agate and marbling at about 10x.

One partition of rock into blocks, by joint plane families or by cells, each with its own lift, tilt and bedding, and a weathering density that opens joints and rounds corners near the surface. Covers cliffs, tors and faulted country.

Plane family blocks, with joints opening and corners rounding near a density surface, plus tilted bedded slabs. Together they are the cliff and tor look noise never gives. 17x to 36x in 3D, so aim for near surface use and watch the slab form's cost.

A meander loop that cuts into any terrain, with an overhanging outer bank and flights of terraces from its past positions. River valleys stay the weakest part of noise terrain, and these give them a real profile.
Canyons with geomorphically placed overhangs and terrace flights, both from one meander plan with a few taps. 12x to 13x, and nothing else in the set gives river valleys that are true 3D.

Column rooted 3D figures on a height or density with no placement pass: trees, stalactites, crystal clusters. Shape enum over a shared root search. Cost runs 10x to 78x, so this node most needs a batch level bound test to skip rock and sky.

Detail in the frame of a density's own surface: flutes down walls, drips at ceilings and floors, crystals on any normal. Voxel terrain has no equivalent to ErosionFilter without this. Ship the flutes first, they are by far the cheapest.

names: StreakSmear: Direction Mode {Fixed, Angle Source, Contour, Downhill} and a Guide source

items.why: Name it what Substance users search for. Fixed taps along or across a flow, Mean, Min and Max accumulate, Quality tap count from 10 up. Keep it easy to find even if it shares code with DomainWarpFlow.

items.node: StreakSmear: Direction Mode {Fixed, Angle Source, Contour, Downhill} and a Guide source
items.why: StreakSmear only has a fixed direction today. Add the modes instead of a second and third line integral node. Same Taps member, and cost scales with it. Taps against detail scale is the main user trap, so document it. curl-steered-grain stays a SteerablePerlin mode.
Painterly and fur strokes on a chosen field: rotate frames for cheap fur, or ShearFrame for strokes with no singular centres. One entry point instead of four near-identical comb nodes.

Spatially varying rotation and scale without swirl, at two source evals, and it works on a 4D plane. Varying the frame directly is what swirls. Bins are a known trick, and the blend band's double exposure is a fair price. Fix band at 1 and keep the scale step at 1 or below, per its notes.

Both need the same density taps and gradient. One gives a downhill frame for 3D flutes on overhangs and cave walls, the other a signed depth for soil and rock rinds. This is what a heightfield engine gets for free and a density engine does not have.
ErosionFilter's stripe kernel steered by the density's own gradient on any isosurface, overhangs included. It carries the library's best node into 3D, and I know of no equivalent anywhere.
Measuring a stamp through the inverse of a warp or flow is one idea. Static gives andamento paving, Time gives rigid beads carried by a flow.

Flooded caves and mountain lakes at any altitude with consistent barriers. Very few engines have this and those that do wrote it by hand. It is still promising: vol is messy and it pays a 27 site search.

Exact land, ore and cave fractions. Costs under 2x plus the source. The Gaussian lattice mode gives the exact marginal, the remap gives any histogram. SplineRemap needs hand tuned knots and does not guarantee the fraction.

Both are CellularLookup with a richer read of the source. Members on a node users know beat two new ones, and Pull 1, Bevel 0, Slope 0 is today's flat lookup. One source eval for the lens. Slope leaves the source's range and tears meshes at cell walls, so it needs a documented gain.
One metric slot on the cell search: per-site ellipse, wind-biased cone, or per-lane flow stretch. Peacock scales, leaded feathers and muscle fibres are presets of the same member.

Measured 449 ns against 972 ns for the same material with one search per channel. Cell id, edge distance and lookup from one search is the normal engine request. Needs care with GeneratorCache style memo under threads.

Constant-width lines with weight from hillshade turn any graph into a print. May live as a SurfaceProbe output. Compare it with Oscillator's Engraving preset first; I did not see the two side by side.

One own-cell crater hierarchy: children on the owner's floor, size and density from a Level hybrid, a gully output for walls, a rim mask for boulders. This is what StampLayers should grow into for moons and Mars.

A table of reflections plus circle inversion covers wallpaper, polyhedral and hyperbolic folds. Its presence completes kaleido-stamp's merge into StampScatter, which currently waits on it. ChiralWallpaper keeps the chiral groups.
Both go past the forward step that every warp in the library uses. The fixed point is the affordable default; overfold's top-layer and count outputs are an expensive mode, honest about its 391x.

Barchans with a wind hybrid, a Supply map that takes them to ridges, and ripples that follow the base gradient and fade on slip faces. A complete desert node, and the ripple pass is useful on any terrain.

The same L2 partition idea. Exact marginal in Uniform and Coverage, and plates at high Hardness with no cell search. Keep only outputs that hold the range, since simplex-plates' Gaussian output reaches -1.33 to 1.44.
Two noises and a jittered lattice in value space give hair and cable at under 3x Perlin. Steered tube channels are one way to feed the same kernel, so they are not a second node.

Both iterate a position map on purpose past the point of good behaviour and read what folds: damped gives crumpled foil, overshoot gives fingerprints in basins. One loop, two modes, Warp and scalar outputs.

Leaves with true vein hierarchy and whorled crowns, stacked with contact shadow. A leaf litter or ground cover height and opacity mask without a modelled scatter, at 17x. No other noise library has it.
Value plus gradient from one evaluation helps every slope-aware node in the lab, which today pays for finite differences. The fractal and the crater gullies are the first users, not the point.
Octave combine rules beyond the sum: running product with voids, soft winner take all, order statistics. FBm can never produce a good grunge mask, and these look aged out of the box.

All iterate a fixed map from the sample and read orbit statistics. A Map enum with noise-fed parameters gives foam lace, lightning veins, chrome and zebra islands, a whole chaos palette for about one kernel.
O(1) near-equal-area cells on the sphere with Lookup and stamp outputs. It is the base that crater, biome and placement work on a planet needs.
Puts any 2D-only graph, Dendry and ErosionFilter included, on a planet with no pole or seam for 3 evals. Nothing else opens the existing node set to planets.
Ridge, valley, peak and hollow as soft masks from any height tree. Slope alone cannot place scree in hollows or snow on ridges. Bake only at this cost, and that is acceptable.
Exports what a warp knows: stretch, fold, rotation, tangent angle. Immediately lovely as filaments and strokes, and the same Jacobian feeds advected-scatter and metric-waves.
A Damage hybrid that opens cracks parent-first and lifts plate edges into peeled curls with substrate. Mask driven wear for materials and time driven reveals for VFX, and one damage map drives both.

items.text: hard-core-cellular, blue-noise-scatter, isolated-extrema-noise, quota-cells, pebble-pack, thin-spots, halftone-spots, cellular-density: round spots chosen per cell, all dots on black at thumbnail size; real StampScatter has Density too
cellular-density, thin-spots, halftone-spots, blue-noise-scatter, hard-core-cellular, quota-cells, pebble-pack, isolated-extrema-noise: sparse whole-disc scatter, differing in the acceptance rule

core.name: RangeProbe
core.one_liner: Conservative lower and upper bound of any node tree over a ball around each lane, through a new interval path in the tree, so a voxel engine can skip chunks that are all air or all rock for the price of a few octaves.
core.core_note: New virtual GenRange(seed, r, pos..., lo&, hi&) on Generator, plus about 20 interval rules for stock nodes and macro support; nodes with no rule fall back to their native range, or to +-inf, meaning no culling. Payoff is chunks skipped, measured in numbers, not a look.
core.why_new: Hard made easy, and an open request. FN2 issue 121 asks for a tree's min and max and the answer is there is no way, only the min and max of generated points. FNL issue 18 and 32 ask the same; issue 32 shows Perlin going past its stated bound by hand, so the rules need checking. FN2 issue 57 asks to see the height bounds. Voxel Tools for Godot ships exactly this: range analysis treats a block as all air or all matter past sdf_clip_threshold, runs on subdivisions, and uses an execution map to skip nodes. Minecraft's density functions have range_choice, an if-then-else on a computed value, which a bound could short cut. A voxel optimisation write-up recommends sampling before filling a chunk, which is unsafe without a bound. Nearest here: StencilFilter Dilate and Erode sample taps with no guarantee. Output Min/Max members are global, not local.
core.risks: Tightness: warps and products widen fast, so a very warped graph culls little. Rigorous Lipschitz constants for lab nodes are work; any wrong rule causes real holes, so random search for violations must be part of the test suite. Adding a virtual to every node is a maintainer call. Also speeds up nothing if the game does not organise work per chunk.
core.smallest_test: Scalar: density = FBm5 + Gradient y plus a Min with a 2 octave cave field, chunks 32^3 on a 512^3 world. Print percent of chunks classified, false claims against dense evaluation (must be 0), and cost per classified chunk against a full chunk.

core.name: AnalyticGradient
core.one_liner: Value and gradient of a whole node tree by the chain rule through a new path, falling back to finite differences for any node without a rule, read through one node per channel at the cost of one evaluation.
core.core_note: New virtual GenGrad(seed, pos..., g[D]) on Generator with a finite-difference default, chain-rule rules per node, and a thread_local channel cache as in GeneratorCache. Payoff is cost and step-free gradients. Same interface as GenJet in jet-fractal, which is the visual demonstration of it: build one, not both. Should share macro work with RangeProbe.
core.why_new: Hard made easy, and on the maintainer's own list. FN2 issue 119: Auburn says it is on the to do list, and users ask to help. FN2 issue 2: coherent noise with derivatives for fractals. FNL issue 151: gradients are expensive by sampling, Auburn defers it to FN2. Quilez reports up to 6x on volumetric clouds and needing normals at every raymarch step. Bevy's bevy_noised does this to keep CPU and GPU heights equal. Nearest here: SurfaceProbe samples, FractalDerivative has an analytic basis for itself only, the k1 GradientNoise kernel stops at the kernel. Single float output is what blocks everyone and the channel plus cache pattern solves it inside the existing model. It would also make ErosionFilter, TubeNoise, SurfaceProbe, CausticWeb and DomainWarpFlow cheaper and free them from the far coordinate step problem, wherever their Source has rules.
core.risks: A lot of rules to maintain, and each new node needs one or inherits the slow path. Warp Jacobians are real work; trees dominated by warps get little. A thread_local cache needs care with tree edits, as GeneratorCache already does. Stencil smoothing was hiding hairline singularities on some lab nodes, so some presets may look worse with exact gradients.
core.smallest_test: Hand write GenGrad in scalar for Perlin, FBm, Add, Remap, DomainScale. Compare with central differences at a tiny step at 1e6 random points: relative error. Then time 3 outputs with the cache against a 4 eval stencil in fnlab bench on a real tree.

core.name: AxisCache
core.one_liner: Minecraft's flat_cache and interpolated markers for FastNoise: a thread local memo that lets a 3D chunk compute its 2D heightmap subtree once per column, or an expensive 3D subtree on sparse levels with a vertical lerp, without changing what the function returns.
core.core_note: A thread_local direct-mapped memo keyed per lane on (generator id, seed, coordinates), with a global epoch bumped by any Set call. Speed only: the look is identical to RemoveDimension in Drop Axis mode.
core.why_new: Hard made easy, speed only. Stock: GeneratorCache holds one batch, so it cannot help a row or column pattern. RemoveDimension still recomputes per voxel. People split trees by hand and combine in their own code, which loses the graph. Evidence read: Minecraft's density functions have flat_cache, cache_2d, cache_once, cache_all_in_cell and interpolated markers for this kind of saving, with terrain shaped in 2D splines above 3D density. r/VoxelGameDev reports 3.5 s to noise a 64x64 chunk in Godot, and a Roblox user found that interpolating 3D noise made the time almost worse, so it must be done carefully. FN2 issue 129 and 73 compare speed with Lite. Issue 163 shows graph users do care about skipped work.
core.risks: Cache hazards: float keys need exact grid repeats, so a tree with non repeating lanes pays probe cost and gains nothing. TLS size across SIMD feature sets and threads. Global epoch is a small API addition. Mixed lane ordering in GenPositionArray can thrash the table. Purists may prefer this inside GenUniformGrid; it stays a node so a graph can mark exactly the subtrees that matter.
core.smallest_test: On a real density tree: Add(Gradient y, DomainAxisScale over an FBm5 2D subtree) in fnlab bench style at 32^3 and 34^3, with and without. Then a 100 ns ErosionFilter subtree. Expect 5x to 30x on the subtree part. Also run the check for parity between hit and miss paths.

core.name: BatchGate
core.one_liner: The only legal 'stop early' in this execution model: skip a whole batch's call to an expensive Detail source when no lane needs it (FS::AnyMask), with output bit-identical to the Fade it replaces.
core.core_note: Whole-batch skip of an expensive input via FS::AnyMask, bit-identical to the Fade it replaces. No Generator change. Payoff is cost only, and only on x-contiguous grids, not on scattered positions.
core.why_new: The handbook says per-lane early-out is impossible and everything costs its worst case; whole-batch skipping is the loophole the library already uses inside CellFrame (if AnyMask(site.d2 < slot)) but never offers to a graph. Fade and HeightBlend always evaluate both inputs. IsoFocusFractal bakes the idea into one fractal; BatchGate gives it to any subgraph. Nearest: fade, height-blend, iso-focus-fractal.
core.risks: Zero gain on scattered positions and the user may expect per-lane savings; any reordering of float ops between branches would break parity; a Control that is itself expensive erases the benefit (keep it to the cheap octaves).
core.smallest_test: Real node: fnlab bench Fade(FBm3, FBm10, band mask) against BatchGate on the same tree at --scale 1 and at a 4x zoom; check must show bit parity between the two trees.

dropped.name: InvertedStamp (Apollonian craters)
dropped.why: The algorithm is bubble-invert's (own-cell sphere, inversion that is the identity at the rim, eps cap, 1 or 2 iterations, then evaluate a Source), and it renders today as DomainInvert(Source=StampLayers crater), so it needs no new kernel and no prototype.
dropped.control_worth_keeping: A lattice scale per iteration: InvertedStamp's second iteration uses the next finer own-cell lattice, where bubble-invert iterates on one lattice. Two nested DomainInvert nodes reach this today.

dropped.name: HorizonProbe
dropped.why: horizon-shadow's AO mode is the same formula (per direction the max of (h - h0)/t over radial taps, then occ += H/sqrt(1 + H^2), out = 1 - occ/M), and the node plan already records that RayMarch overlaps this seed.
dropped.control_worth_keeping: Cavity output (occlusion minus its value at a wider radius). A settable Directions count with a golden-angle rotation per ring: RayMarch AO is hard-coded to 4 directions. The 3D density form: fraction of 14 fixed-direction taps inside solid.

dropped.name: LeakStreaks
dropped.why: The kernel is StreakSmear's Max tap loop along a direction with a fade per tap, whose rust runs and rain stains are the same look, and the rest composes today as Multiply(StreakSmear(Max, Source=directional difference of Height), column noise), with Length as a hybrid for per-column length.
dropped.control_worth_keeping: Ledge source from consecutive tap differences, h_i - h_(i-1), which shares taps (N+1 evals, where the graph needs about 2N). Gamma fade per tap. Built-in per-column Breakup and fade from 1D noise. A Period option, since Up has no meaning through GenTileable2D's torus.

dropped.name: CliffBands
dropped.why: contour-scarp's multi-band option is this algorithm: band index floor((h - L0)/spacing), first-order distance (h - level)/|grad h|, then a cliff and talus profile in world units, giving stacked cliff bands of constant width.
dropped.control_worth_keeping: Hardness hybrid modulating band spacing per lane. Curvature-based gradient floor 0.5 h (|hxx| + |hyy|) from the same taps, in place of a fixed Eps. Central differences with the exact-step divisor.

plan2.honesty: Nothing in this plan has been built. Every look is the prototype's look, seen through a scalar harness. Every cost is an estimate, marked as one, scaled from real fnlab benches of round 1 nodes where one exists. Prototypes with scalar rejects flatter the port, so estimates here assume no per lane early out. Judge scores are from the 218 prototype panel in ranked.json and were not redone.

nodes.why_difficulty: Six rules in one octave loop, a rotating gradient for Morse, and range constants to measure per rule and dimension. Each rule is small.
nodes.why: Five of six judges name this group in build_next and the sixth lists it next. It is the biggest visual jump over stock FBm. Five prototypes measure at FBm cost and share a loop, so one node replaces five. Forecast joins because its Detail weight is the Spectrum weight plus a known tail, and three judges want it for LOD.

members.name: Source
members.note: Unconnected: built in Perlin from GradientNoise.inl at Feature Scale, with its analytic gradient. Connected: any node, Feature Scale unused, sampled once per octave, or D + 1 times per octave in Morse. Test connection as HeightBlend does: mSource.base.

members.name: Rule
members.note: Chosen outside the loop, per node not per lane.

members.name: Octaves
members.note: 2 to 16. Every octave is paid for even at near zero weight, except Forecast on coherent batches.

members.name: Lacunarity
members.note: 2.03 so octave lattice zeros do not nest.

members.name: Gain
members.note: Read once at the base position, per lane. Presets: Focus 0.65, Sparse 0.85, Spectrum bell 1.

members.name: Octave Rotation
members.note: Fixed rotation composed each octave: golden angle in 2D, the prototype's Rodrigues matrix in 3D, golden angle in the (x,y) and (z,w) planes in 4D.

members.name: Amount
members.note: Morse: Lock, 0 is classic FBm, 1 keeps the base octave's topology. Focus: gate width, default 0.55 in presets. Spectrum: bell width in octaves, 0 or below turns the bell off. Cascade: Intermittency, 3 in presets. Clamped at 0.

members.name: Level
members.note: Focus: output value where detail lives. Spectrum: octave index of the bell peak, 2.2 in presets. Forecast: threshold in units of the full fractal's std.

members.name: Detail
members.note: Spectrum and Forecast: octaves in use, fractional, weight sat( Detail - i ). The default is off for Spectrum; Forecast presets set it.

members.name: Sharpness
members.note: Sparse: how many times v^2 is squared, 0 to 3. The prototype's 4 underflows.

members.name: Max Slope
members.note: Morse with a connected Source: largest gradient of one octave in source units per world unit. For Perlin about 2.2 / Feature Scale; batch 0 measures the real constant, which goes in the member text.

members.name: Sample Distance
members.note: Morse with a connected Source: Probe::Jet radius in world units. About 1/50 of the Source's Feature Scale.

members.name: Source Std
members.note: Forecast: std of one octave. Batch 0 measures it for stock sources, the table goes in the member text. Prototype's perlin2 0.3047, perlin3g 0.2203.

members.name: Softness
members.note: Forecast: added to the tail variance so Coverage stays C0 at full Detail.

members.name: Output
members.note: Forecast only. Other rules ignore it.

algorithm: One GenT over P..., FractalFBm's loop: seed increments per octave, pos *= lacunarity. Hybrids are read once before the loop at the base position, because a parent fractal or a scaled position would sample them elsewhere.

Morse: keep G, the accumulated gradient, in the current octave's frame. Each step G = R G / lacunarity. a_i = Gain^i, g2 = |G|^2, l = MaxSlope * a_i * Amount, q = g2 / ( g2 + l^2 + 1e-12 ), hard knee q = q^2 / ( q^2 + ( 1 - q )^2 + 1e-12 ), amp = a_i * q, F += amp n_i, G += amp grad n_i. The first octave has q = 1. Output K F / sqrt( sum a_i^2 ). The soft knee and its enum are dropped: hard is closer to base at Lock 1 (extrema 20-25 against 41-56).

Morse gradient: unconnected uses GradientNoise::Perlin, grad in the octave's frame, MaxSlope the batch 0 constant for that kernel. Connected uses Probe::Jet on Source in the octave's frame, n_i = tapMean, h = Sample Distance. No extra centre tap.

Focus: rem_i = sum of a_j for j >= i, per lane because Gain is hybrid. gate = 1 - smoothstep( 0, Amount * 0.7 * rem_i, |h - lv| ), 1 on the first octave, h += a_i n_i gate, lv = Level * norm * K so Level is in output units. The prototype compared raw h. Output h / ( norm K ).

Spectrum: w_i = Gain^i * sat( Detail - i ) * bell, bell = ( 1 - u^2 / 9 )^3 clamped at 0 with u = ( i - Level ) / Amount, or 1 where Amount <= 0. Compact bell, no Exp. Output K sum( w_i n_i ) * InvSqrt( sum w_i^2 + eps ). Where all weights vanish the output goes to 0 continuously.
Sparse: v = a_i n_i, w = v^2 squared Sharpness times, floored at 1e-30 for denormals, output K sum( w v ) / ( sum w + 1e-20 ).
Cascade: R = 1, I = Amount; each level R *= Max( 0, 1 + I n_i ), I *= 0.8. Output 2 R / ( R + 1 ) - 1. The decay and knee are fixed constants, which removes two members.

Forecast: octave weight w_i = sat( Detail - i ). S = sum a_i w_i n_i. Tail variance V = Std^2 sum a_i^2 ( 1 - w_i^2 ), full variance V0 = Std^2 sum a_i^2, tau = Level sqrt( V0 ). Coverage = Phi( ( S - tau ) / sqrt( V + Softness^2 ) ) mapped to -1..1, Phi by A&S 26.2.17. Floor, Abs closed forms from the prototype, Expected = S, Sigma = sqrt( V / V0 ). Break the loop once no lane has Detail > i, FS::AnyMask: it cannot change a result, so it is legal on position arrays too.
Only the Forecast loop may break early. The others run all octaves.
must_carry: Morse hard knee, not the soft one.
Spectrum's Odd and Cantor patterns stay out: they look the same as All.
Region blends need weights over all window sites, never F2 - F1: the catalogue form jumps along F2 = F3 lines. CellularSmooth is the right soft Level source.
Sparse floors w to avoid denormals. Rotation for all rules, with lacunarity 2.03 kept so octaves do not nest when rotation is off.
nodes.dims: One GenT for 2D, 3D, 4D. GradientNoise::Perlin has all three. The prototypes measured 2D and 3D only, the harness had no 4D path, so 4D is unmeasured until the port. GenTileable2D works through the real 4D form, and rotation is a function of position, so the torus closes. Topology counts exist for 2D only.
nodes.range: VariableRange, native -1..1. Morse and Spectrum K per rule and dimension, measured at the port and clamped: prototypes read Morse -0.851..0.845 at K 1, Spectrum -0.828..0.866 at K 0.72, and 3D lower (std 0.166 against 0.213), so 3D needs its own constant. Focus K 0.36 at Gain 0.65 depends on Gain, so fit K at 0.4, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8 and clamp. Sparse is bounded by the largest |v_i|. Cascade and Coverage are exact by construction. Expected, Floor and Abs are divided by 3 sqrt( V0 ) and clamped.
nodes.continuity: C0 wherever Source is: every weight is a continuous function of position. No window, so no window seams. Morse gate continuous through eps. Focus gate is a smoothstep; prototype c0 3.48 is steep high octaves, 7.48 at 10x the scale. Sparse steep at switch lines, c0 6.15, 8.00 at 10x scale. Cascade is C0 with creases at void edges, by design. Forecast C0 in Detail, so hillshade of a Detail ramp shows faint lines at whole Detail. All prototypes: step shrinks 10x per decade, 0 jumps in scan.
nodes.expected_cost: ESTIMATE, AVX2 ns 2D / 3D / 4D, nothing ported. Scaled from real benches: FractalFBm 4 octaves of Perlin 4.18 / 8.84 / 16.50, K1 Perlin with gradient about 2 / 4 / 8.5 per octave. 6 octaves on Perlin: Spectrum, Sparse, Cascade 7-8 / 15-17 / 28-32. Focus at 7 octaves 8-9 / 17-19 / 33. Morse built in Perlin 13 / 26 / 55. Morse connected Perlin by Jet 19 / 55 / 125. Forecast at Detail 3 about 5-6 / 9-10 / 17, Detail 8 about 11 / 21 / 38. members.name: Mode
members.note: Height is today's node. Surface treats Source as a density, solid above 0, and runs flutes down its isosurface.

members.name: Flute Frequency
members.note: Surface: radians per gully cell, about 4 stripes per cell. Long stripes need this high: at 5 flutes read as lumps, seen in the prototype.

members.name: Surface Band
members.note: Surface: how far from the isosurface flutes reach, in gully cells.

nodes.reuses: Source, Feature Scale (gully cell), Strength (presets 0.03: the prototype's 0.055 was on a density with gain 2.2), Up Axis (gravity runs against it), Sample Distance (Surface multiplies by 0.06 so the shared default 1.33 gives the prototype's 0.08 cells), Output (Height, Delta, Mask), Seed Offset. Stripe Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain, Stripe Frequency, Branching, Slope Reference, Altitude Fade and the Fade members are not read in Surface, and the member text says so.
algorithm: 3D only. probe = Probe::Jet( source, 0.06 * Sample Distance * Feature Scale, x, y, z ): 4 taps on a tetrahedron, S = tapMean, no centre tap. g = probe.gradient.
n = g * InvSqrt( |g|^2 + 1e-8 ). Down = minus Up Axis. t = down - n ( n . down ), L = |t|. b = cross( n, t ) / Max( L, 1e-4 ).

Lattice at Feature Scale, 2^3 corners, quintic weights. Per corner hash h, offset v: phase = Flute Frequency * dot( v, b ) + tau * rnd( h ). re += W cos( phase ), im += W sin( phase ). Value = re / sqrt( re^2 + im^2 + 0.12^2 ).
Mask = ( 1 - smoothstep( 0, Surface Band, |S / |g|| / Feature Scale ) ) * smoothstep( 0.1, 0.4, L ). Output Height: S + Strength * Mask * Value. Delta: Strength * Mask * Value. Mask: 2 Mask - 1.
One flute octave, fixed. Ridged and two octaves shredded in the prototype.
Sincos: PolyMath SinCos per corner first. If the bench is over the estimate, use 3 SinCos of Flute Frequency * b components and corner rotations by angle addition.
2D Mode Surface runs today's Height path, and the member text says so: the prototype's 2D star bursts read worse than what ErosionFilter already does.
must_carry: Corners, not 27 jittered cells: the window is 8 and not 27.
High phase rate per cell. This was the fix that made flutes long.
Strength goes to 0 where L is below 0.1: b has no continuous definition there, and the mask is what keeps the output continuous.
eps 0.12: below it dislocations get steeper, 0.3 softens the stripes.
nodes.dims: 2D: Height path. 3D: the real form, measured in the prototype: z-continuity mean 0.0008, max 0.0112 for dz=1e-3. 4D: not built. The frame needs a cross product, so the 4D Gen runs the 3D form on (x,y,z) with w passed to Source only. It drops out of GenTileable2D in Surface mode, and the description says so. Height mode's existing 4D torus form is unchanged.
nodes.range: Not normalised, like ErosionFilter today: Source plus or minus Strength. No VariableRange. Prototype -1.314..0.904 on a 3D slice with its own gain. Mask exactly -1..1.
nodes.continuity: No jump found. Steep, not jumping: prototype c0 about 2 (straddle 2.12), slice steps 0.03983, 0.00439, 0.00043 for h 1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5. Steep at phasor dislocations where |Z| is small; eps bounds it. Rough sources lower the ratio (dOct=4 straddle 1.15, step 0.0032 at 1e-5). fnlab seams may flag steep segments, so read them with a step sweep before calling any a jump.
nodes.expected_cost: ESTIMATE, AVX2 ns 3D only, nothing ported. Flute part 8-14 ns: 8 corners with hash and sincos, one rsqrt for n, one for b, one sqrt for Z. Prototype said 6-9, real ErosionFilter stripes cost 8 per octave on 9 cells, so the low end is optimistic. Plus 4 Source taps: on 1 octave Perlin 3D about 8.8 ns, so 17-23 total; on 3 octave Perlin FBm (6.58 real) about 26 ns, so 35-40 total. nodes.reuses: Grid Jitter, capped per output below. Edge Width is the strut radius in Strut, presets 0.24. Edge Depth, Levels, Colours and the rest keep their meaning; Facets, Rings, Uniform and Strut do not read Levels or Colours, and the member text says so.
algorithm: Gauge: pass 2 over the sample's stored window, never one centred on the winner: that seams far more (2.46 percent of samples, worst 0.79). g = max over j != owner of 2 dot( x - p_i, p_j - p_i ) / |p_j - p_i|^2 * W_j. Mask the owner out by the denominator.

Window weight W_j, from jigsaw-gauge and voronoi-drum: W_j = min( max( fade( d_j^2 ), box_j ) / fade( F2^2 ), 1 ), fade( d ) = hermite( sat( ( R1^2 - d ) / ( R1^2 - R0^2 ) ) ), R1 = 1.5 - jitter radius, R0 = 0.8 R1, box_j = product over axes of a per axis term, with fr the sample's position in the window's centre column, 0 to 1: low column hermite( sat( ( 1 - fr ) / 0.2 ) ), centre column 1, high column hermite( sat( fr / 0.2 ) ). A site leaving the window then has term 0. F2 comes from CellTopK<2>, and the search caps d^2 at R1^2.
Grid Jitter capped at 0.8 on Facets, Rings, Uniform and Strut, like kWeightJitterMax for Foam. Brute force steps at 0.8: 2D 0.0093 percent worst 0.057 before the weight, 3D none above 1e-3.
Outputs: Facets 1 - 2 g. Rings t = fract( g Ring Count ), |2 t - 1| * 2 - 1. Uniform 2 g^D - 1, per cell exactly uniform. Strut below.

Strut: top 3 by CellTopK, no second pass. a = F2^2 - F1^2, b = F3^2 - F1^2, e = 1.15 sqrt( a^2 + b^2 - a b ) / ( F1 + F2 + F3 ), output 1 - 2 min( e / Max( Edge Width, 1e-4 ), 1 ). Uses no site labels, so it cannot jump at an owner swap. The catalogue form jumped 8661 crossings, worst 1.215.

Bend: top 3 with d^2 capped. lo, hi by hash order, qh = mix( h0 ^ h1, 3 ). s0 = ( d_lo^2 - d_hi^2 ) / 2. env = smoothstep( 0, 0.45, d3^2 - d2^2 ). dir = hash direction from qh, projected into the wall plane in 3D and 4D. t = dot( dir, x - midpoint ). wob = sin( f t + ph ) + 0.35 sin( 2.13 f t + ph2 ). s = s0 + Bend Amount env wob. Distance |s| / den, den fading from |q_hi - q_lo| to a constant with env. This replaces CellWalls when Bend Amount is connected or above 0.
Bend Amount 0 and unconnected must take today's path exactly.
must_carry: The sample's window for pass 2, not the winner's.
No dmin floor: it is not C0 (c0 1.10). Jitter bounds the closest pair.
Per site window weight on the gauge. Plain probe read 8.00 on Facets while straddle read 1.83, step 0.077 at every h. This is the recurring round 2 fault, fixed.
Bend's denominator fades with env. Dividing by |grad s| jumped at F2 identity changes (c0 1.0, slope 1918).
Bend caps d^2: without it the top 3 search has real jumps on window lines, c0 1.3-1.6 by the offset probe only.
Strut form 2, never form 0 or the true line form 1.

members.note: SeedValue. Two leaves with different Salt give independent values from one seed.

members.name: Source

members.name: Seed Source
members.note: SeedRoute. Read at the real position, with the incoming seed.

members.name: Quantise
members.note: SeedRoute. s = Seed Source * Quantise, k = Floor( s ). A CellularValue key with large Quantise gives one seed per cell.

members.name: Mode

algorithm: SeedValue: GenT ignores positions. h = hash( seed, Salt ), mixed, value = hash to -1..1. With Choices: Floor( ( value + 1 ) / 2 * Choices ) / ( Choices - 1 ) * 2 - 1. One hash and about six ops.

It needs no parent work: hybrid members are sampled per lane, and the seed passed down is what the leaf hashes. TileDomain, StampScatter, CellFrame and ExchangeFoam already pass a per lane or stride seed. FractalFBm reads Gain before it increments seed, so a Gain from SeedValue sees the tile's seed.
SeedRoute Hard: s = Seed Source( seed, pos ) * Quantise, k = Convert( Floor( s ) ), Source( seed ^ hash( k, Salt ), pos ). Keep |k| below 2^24.

SeedRoute Blend: t = s - k, tt = smoothstep( t ) * pi / 2, a = Source( seed ^ H( k ) ), b = Source( seed ^ H( k + 1 ) ), output Mean + ( a - Mean ) cos( tt ) + ( b - Mean ) sin( tt ), PolyMath SinCos. Cos and sin weights, not a lerp.
must_carry: Cos and sin weights: std spread over t 0.30 percent on FBm against 29.43 percent for a lerp.
SeedValue has no position term. It tiles and costs the same in any dimension.
Output of a per element value only shows where the parent's bevel or weight is above 0: the prototype's border test reads 0.000 change on mortar. Keep that test.
nodes.dims: Any dimension through one GenT, no window. SeedRoute forwards positions. Measured in 2D and 3D. 4D is not measured but has no 4D specific code. Tiling follows Source and Seed Source.
nodes.range: SeedValue: exact Output Min..Max, VariableRange. SeedRoute Hard: follows Source. SeedRoute Blend: follows Source up to a factor sqrt 2 at t = 0.5 for correlated sources or a wrong Mean: -0.612..1.310 on Ridged with Mean 0. Not clamped, because it is a modifier, and the description says so.
nodes.continuity: SeedValue is constant for a given seed: it jumps exactly where a parent's seed changes, which a parent hides under mortar or a weight. SeedRoute Hard jumps on the level sets of the quantised field, by design: 1.135 / 1.090 / 1.090 without mortar, hidden with F2 - F1 mortar. SeedRoute Blend is C0 for continuous Source and Seed Source: at t = 1 sin = 1, and the next segment starts with cos = 1 on the same seed. Measured 0.00667 / 0.00067 / 0.00007.
nodes.expected_cost: ESTIMATE, AVX2 ns. SeedValue under 1 ns in any dimension; prototype could not separate it from noise: 288.5 against 289.1 ns scalar across 7 reads. SeedRoute Hard: 1 ns plus Seed Source plus Source. Blend: about 1.5 ns plus Seed Source plus 2 x Source. The cost is the user's graph.

nodes.reuses: Radius, Damping, Output. Pipe and Rope work on all new forms. Rope's flutes run straight on sideways wires, no helix: the prototype took the twist from world y.
algorithm: Floor: per pair solve as today, then l0 = ( e n0 - b n1 ) / det, l1 = ( a n1 - b n0 ) / det, r = j0 l0 + j1 l1 per axis, len = |r|. sd = smax( len - R, -r_up - Floor R, 0.25 R ), up is Y. Network takes Min of the pair sds. One sqrt per pair. r.y comes from the same solve. When Floor is 0 keep today's squared measure path, it is the cheap one.

Bedding: y' = y + DipX x + DipZ z + Fold Perlin2( x, z at 0.3 ), value and gradient from one 2D Perlin visit. Planes m_c = T ( c + J ( hash( c ) - 0.5 ) ). n1 = y' - m_c in world units, one candidate per plane, Min over the 4 planes around the sample. grad n1 = grad y' for every plane, so a, b, e, det are shared and a candidate costs 3 multiplies plus a sqrt. Three noise channels from PerlinChannels<3>. Channels 0 and 1, each paired with n1, give 2 gallery families per plane. The 3 channel pairs give riser families, radius 0.7 R. Per plane radius jitter 0.35 and coverage 1 fixed.

Steer: own lattice loop, used only when Steer > 0. u = normalised Direction. Fixed lattice rotation, 9 multiplies for p and 9 for u, because a vertical direction otherwise shows rows of columns. Per corner: metric G d = e1 d + ( e0 - e1 ) ( u . d ) u, e1 = lerp( isotropic, 0.15, Steer ), sum rule 3.6 in 3D as t_steered_tube, weight = lattice weights * fade( d . G d ), then one dot and one Jacobian term per channel. Distance is Gauss-Newton with G frozen.

Strands: f = K ( n0, n1 ) + offset from one PerlinChannels<2>, 3x3 jittered sites in value space in every dimension, 3 sites in Sheet. Levenberg: A += lambda, C += lambda, lambda = 0.001 ( A + C ). Reff = min( R, 0.5 / ( K sigmaMax ) ), sigmaMax^2 includes lambda. Output clamps at 2 Reff, which hides the value space window. Damping is unused here.
All four share Output code from distance to Tunnel, Distance, Pipe, Rope. Length ignores them.
must_carry: Min of per pair sd, never Select on min |r| then one sd.
No saw in Bedding. Saw forms jump: entry form 16890 of 37744 crossings at R 0.45, worst 0.57; Gauss-Newton saw worst 1.19. The Min over planes form measured zero over 0.01 at R up to 0.45.
Keep Apart is fixed at 0.5: at 2 the wires seam, 549 crossings over 0.01, worst 0.83.
Levenberg, not a det floor: on the 3D plane c0 2.199 to 7.807.

nodes.why: Any subgraph tiles at any period, warps and fractals included, which per node Period members cannot do. Material artists ship tiling maps first. Round 1 passed on it, saying to try the Period member first: that now exists, and it stops at lattice sources. Few members, a real 4D form.

members.name: Period
members.note: Period X, Y, Z, W in world units, 0 is off for that axis. Default 256 on X and Y, 0 on Z and W. Not hybrid.

members.name: Blend Fraction
members.note: Share of the period used for the crossfade. Smaller shows less ghosting on sharp sources, at the price of a quicker fade.

members.name: Flatten

members.name: Mean

algorithm: Per tiled axis: u = x - P Floor( x / P ), x0 = u, x1 = u - P, w = smoothstep( P ( 1 - B ), P, u ). Untiled axis passes through with one branch of the cube.
out = sum over the cube of W_i S_i( x_i ), W_i the product of w or 1 - w per axis. With Flatten: Mean + sum W_i ( S_i - Mean ) / sqrt( sum W_i^2 ), one Sqrt, one Reciprocal.

Fixed recursion over tiled axes through a pack. Batch skip: if no lane has w > 0 on an axis, skip that axis's x1 calls. FS::AnyMask, per batch, so it cannot change a result. Worst case bill stays. On grids most batches skip.
Seed unchanged across copies.
must_carry: Flatten default off, per the maintainer lens and the measured overshoot.
Period and Blend are not hybrid: a varying period does not close.
Positions stay in [ -P, P ), which also keeps far coordinates sane: -0.868..0.790 at 4e4.

Inside GenTileable2D the torus would be tiled again, which is harmless but costs 16 calls, so the description says use one or the other.

nodes.why_difficulty: One spot renderer and five order functions. HardCore's hash block and Quota's Morton descent are the two hard parts, and both have measuring tools to copy.
nodes.why: Six prototypes read as dots on black and differ only in how a spot is accepted. Every judge says collapse them. The ability is real for voxel and terrain: even spacing, exact quotas and coverage that thins whole spots are what foliage and rocks need, and each team writes this by hand. The Rank output with an IGN or R2 order is the low discrepancy dither, so it needs no White change.

members.name: Order
members.note: How a cell's spot gets its acceptance value.

members.name: Coverage
members.note: Read once at the sample, so a connected node costs one eval and spots shrink away whole instead of being cut. Quota's exact count holds only where this is constant, and only in aligned blocks.

members.name: Radius
members.note: In cells. HardCore discs never touch up to ( 2 - jitter ) / 2. Clamped at 1.5 - jitter / 2 so a spot stays inside the window.

members.name: Radius Jitter
members.note: Per spot shrink.

members.name: Height Jitter
members.note: Per spot height.

members.name: Grid Jitter
members.note: HardCore's spacing is at least 2 - jitter cells. Quota uses the free room instead and ignores it.

members.name: Softness
members.note: Width of a spot's switch on as Coverage rises. Small: dots of one size whose density follows Coverage. Near 1: every dot grows.

members.name: Profile
members.note: Lens 1 - t^4 has a finite rim slope and needs no sqrt. Pits are Output Min above Output Max.

members.name: Output
members.note: Rank is flat per cell and jumps by design: IGN Rank is the dither mask. Distance is F1 of active sites, not available on Quota, where it returns Spots.

algorithm: Random, IGN, R2, HardCore: 3^D window of jittered sites via CellWindow. Per site an order value o. on = smoothstep( o, o + Softness, Coverage ( 1 + Softness ) ). r = Radius ( 1 - Radius Jitter rnd ) on^0.5, height = ( 1 - Height Jitter rnd ) on^0.5. t = d / r, value = height profile( t ). Output Max over sites, 2 value - 1. Masked divide guards r = 0.
Height scales with on, so a spot reaches 0 before it vanishes. Max of domes, never the nearest site's height: picking the nearest jumped (c0 1.46) when discs overlap.
Random o = hash01( CellMix( h ) ).

IGN: integer cell wrapped to 16 bits, o = fract( 52.9829189 fract( 0.06711056 x + 0.00583715 y ) ), the 3D form as t_low_discrepancy_dither. Seed shifts x by 8 hash bits, so seeds are translations of one pattern, and the description says so. R2: o = fract( x a1 + y a2 ), plastic constants in 2D, 3D and from x^5 = x + 1 in 4D.

HardCore: 5^D hash block, a candidate is active when its hash beats all its 3^D - 1 neighbours: an AND of integer compares, no count. Active sites have o = 0 (and pass Coverage through a second hash mix). Inactive contribute 0. 3^D candidates each with a masked distance. Rank output counts neighbours below.

Quota: own cell, no window. L = 6 levels, finest digit to the top of the rank, per level one hash and a bijection from an xor mask and a table of invertible GF(2) matrices (6 in 2D, 8 hand checked in 3D and 4D). Spot uses the free room of its own cell as jitter, radius at most 0.4.
Distance: F1 of active sites, clamped at 1 + ( 1 - jitter ) / 2, the nearest a site outside the window can be.
must_carry: Max of domes.
Lens rim 1 - t^4, not a sphere cap: the cap's slope is unbounded, c0 2.9.
HardCore's raw hash needs the mix (hmix=1) only for the rank key's independence: chi2 was fine for both; keep the mix.
Quota's finest digit on top, the matrix table checked for singular entries: a singular matrix in the first 3D table broke 512 of 4096 hashes, and only the block test caught it.
IGN cell wrap to 16 bits, or far coordinates lose the fraction. No Shuffle: it lets live cells touch, 0.272 against 0.001.
nodes.dims: HardCore, Random, IGN, R2: 2D and 3D measured, 4D on an oblique plane. HardCore in 4D is 625 hashes and 6480 compares: real but a bake path, about 200 ns or more. Quota 2D, 3D, 4D all measured with the quota test, 4D mask on a plane. Dither 4D not written; R4 constants exist. GenTileable2D runs through the real 4D forms for Random, HardCore, Quota; IGN and R2 do not tile by nature, and the description says so.

Rank jumps by design, every cell edge. No lattice line seam: a site at reach has r <= reach, and an inactive site contributes 0 on both sides.

A port pays all candidates. Random, IGN, R2 Spots 5-7 / 15-20 / 55-65 plus Coverage. HardCore Spots 7-10 / 30-40 / 200-260. Quota Rank 1.5-2.5 in any dimension, Quota Spots 2-3.5. IGN Rank under 1. nodes.why_difficulty: Triangle location, a homothety chain with gap circles, per triangle affine frames, and Kuhn tets in 3D, all with no branches.
nodes.why: Exact non overlap in closed form with a wide size range. Overlap is the usual flaw of stamped pebbles and nothing stock can guarantee this. Ranks 8 and 15, and three judges name the same node. One wrapper turns circles into flow aligned ellipses, so they are one node.

members.name: Frame
members.note: Circle: true circles. Flow: blend of the Steiner frame with Angle and Aspect, the prototype's mode 2. Fit: the largest ellipse in each triangle, no voids, shows the triangulation.

members.name: Aspect Min
members.note: Flow. Coverage falls with aspect: 0.724 at 1, 0.668 at 2, 0.589 at 3.

members.name: Aspect Max
members.note: Flow.

members.name: Angle
members.note: Flow, radians. Read once per lane at the located triangle's centroid, so a connected node costs one eval and the ellipse never tears.

members.name: Angle Jitter
members.note: Flow: hashed per triangle.

members.name: Blend
members.note: Flow: share of the Steiner frame. Falls back to Fit per triangle if the blended matrix's determinant nears 0.

members.name: Grid Jitter
members.note: Capped at 0.33 in 3D to keep Kuhn tets valid, which leaves a faint arrangement.

members.name: Depth
members.note: 0 to 3. Corner circle levels.

members.name: Fill Gaps
members.note: 2D only: circles in the curved gaps. Depth 2 with Mask gives a gasket.

members.name: Gap
members.note: Shrink factor on every grain.

members.name: Height
members.note: Dome: height per unit of minor axis, so small grains sit low.

members.name: Blot
members.note: Spiky flake outline, 0.45 in presets. Uses complex powers of the unit vector, 3rd and 5th harmonics, no trig.

members.name: Period
members.note: Native tiling in 2D: wrap lattice indices in the hash, as TileDomain does. Not prototyped, low risk. 0 off.

members.name: Output
members.note: Mask and Id jump by design. SDF dropped: it needs all 8 triangles at about 3x the cost.

algorithm: 2D: jittered square lattice, one diagonal per cell, 8 candidate triangles. Locate the one holding the sample by max( min( lambda ) ), Select its 3 corners. Every circle lies inside its triangle, so Dome, Lens, Mask, Id need only that triangle. Pixel identical to scanning all 8: max diff 0 measured.

Frame: per triangle 2x2 matrix S. Map 3 vertices and the sample by S, run the circle code on the mapped triangle unchanged. Affine maps keep tangency and containment, so grains cannot overlap whatever S each triangle chose. Circle: S = I. Fit: S maps the triangle to equilateral, one divide by its det. Flow: lerp( Fit, diag( 1, a ) R( -theta ), 1 - Blend ).

Circles: incircle I, r. Corner circle: q = ( D - r ) / ( D + r ), D = |corner - I|, r_k = r q, centre = corner + ( I - corner ) q. Depth repeats q. Gap circles: 1/sqrt( r3 ) = 1/sqrt( r1 ) + 1/sqrt( r2 ), foot at 2 sqrt( r1 r3 ) along the edge.

Value: Max over the triangle's grains of height profile( t ), profile 1 - t^4. Height from the world minor semi-axis, closed form 2x2 largest singular value (2 sqrts). Output 2 value - 1 with background -1.

3D: Kuhn tets, 48 per cell. Locate one by sorting fractional coordinates, not by scanning: 382 ns against 1623 ns scalar. Insphere and homothetic corner spheres at one sqrt each. S = diag( 1, a, b ) R^T from a hash quaternion (PolyMath). No gap spheres.
Angle is read at the located triangle's centroid: positions Selected per lane, one source eval.
must_carry: One triangle path. It saved 3.7x in scalar and is pixel identical.
Lens rim 1 - t^4, not a sphere cap (c0 2.91).
Blend falls back per triangle, constant inside a triangle, so seamless.
Hash for frames separate from jitter bits.

Prototype scaled by 10:1 from scalar gave 13-18 for circles, 8-12 was the entry's guess for ellipses. No early out: all grains of the triangle are always computed. 3D Dome 45-60. nodes.reuses: Grid Jitter: in Hex, 1.0 maps to the audited limit below, not to Square's radius. Distance Function, Distance Index, Return Type, Size Jitter, Seed Offset, Feature Scale.
algorithm: Add HexWindow<D> beside CellWindow<D> in CellWindow.inl, same Load( i, site ) interface and a Sites array. CellWalls and CellTopK become templates on the array size. Additive, with default arguments so today's calls compile unchanged, since SpotScatter reads this file in the same batch. CellWindow<D> output stays bit identical.
2D: axial coordinates, cube round branch free by Select on the largest rounding error, self plus 6 table offsets, 7 candidates.

3D and 4D: for sublattice s in 0, 1: floor( p / a - s / 2 ), corners by bit test, 2 x 2^D = 16 and 32 candidates, no search or sort. a = 2^(1/3) and 2^(1/4) for unit density, so Feature Scale keeps its meaning. Second sublattice hashes with a different seed.

Jitter: shell jitter as FastNoise does (jmode=1), no pow. Effective radius = Grid Jitter * limit, limit 0.29 of the nearest neighbour spacing in 2D and 0.2 in 3D and 4D, where edge output has no measured error. Clamp hybrid Grid Jitter at 1.

Stock nodes: at Lattice Hex, a new GenT path through HexWindow, computing the same Return Types. Metric: Euclidean and EuclideanSquared. Test the others in the first hour with the jump scan; if they seam, Hex uses EuclideanSquared whatever is set, and the member text says so.
Distance Index 2 and 3: 7 candidates do not guarantee F3 and F4 in 2D. Test; if wrong, clamp the index at 1 under Hex and say so.

CellularLookup: q = X + off * smoothstep( 0, Bevel, edge ) * Pull, off the vector to the owner's site, edge = ( F2 - F1 ) / 2. One Source eval. At Pull 1, unconnected Bevel 0, run today's path: it must stay bit identical.

Metadata: append these members in each derived class's MetadataT after its existing members, not in Cellular<PARENT>'s base MetadataT. Variables and hybrids are stored with their member index, so a member in the base would shift every derived index and break old encoded trees.
must_carry: Shell jitter, not the uniform ball, which needs a pow per site. Look not viewed in the prototype at this setting, so view it.
Audited limits from brute force: 2D F1 up to 0.35, F2-F1 0.35, edge 0.29. 3D F1 0.40, F2-F1 0.25, edge 0.20. 4D F1 0.40. Sample counts are 12000 to 200000, so rare errors could exist.

Bevel continuity: edge goes to 0 at every wall, so the swap of centre happens at t = 0. Fix found in the prototype: a wrong hex face distance read c0 1.00 on 3D BCC.

members.note: Courses: rows of bricks, one hash, no window. 2D only; in 3D and 4D it runs Scatter with boxes in the course frame. Scatter: round stamps in a 3^D window.

algorithm: Q = p + W( p ) in lattice units of Feature Scale. J by central differences of Warp at p: 5 warps in 2D, 7 in 3D, 9 in 4D. Step h = 0.01 / warp frequency, at least 5e-7 times the largest |coordinate|, dividing by the real step after rounding, the law from warp-strain.
Frame: t = J^-1 e_x normalised, n = normalised J^T e_y. Do not use the polar rotation: it tears bricks under shear.

Courses, Eval2C in the prototype: row = Floor( Q.y ). Along a row o.t = tl ( dqx + K dqy ), so the column is the floor of Q.x + K dqy. One hash, no window, no Select chain. Bond is an integer test on row. Bricks exactly tile in first order and give up constant size: they grow and shrink with strain.
Stamp height from the signed distance to the brick in world units: Mortar and Bevel apply in the G metric, so joints keep one width.

Scatter: sites in Q space, 3^D window with per row offset. o = J^-1 ( q - s ). Stamp radius scaled by Min( 1, allow / ( bound * sigma_max * cell ) ), allow = 1.5 - jitter / 2. Max of stamps, each reaching 0 at its edge.
Warp's seed and offset: pass through Warp() as DomainWarpFractal does.

Density is det J.

The maintainer asks to settle how it differs from CellFrame. CellFrame blends K frames with no grout, K evals, soft. CellDomain takes the owner only, hides the jump under grout, 1 eval, hard. members.note: Evaluated once per lane in the frame.

members.note: World: a coherent image reads as broken and shifted, child seed unchanged. Owner: each cell its own take, child seed mixed with the cell id, so SeedValue works.

members.note: In cells, per shard.

members.note: Multiplies the frame's position.

algorithm: CellWindow pass, owner by CellTopK<1>, CellWalls distance d. Then Shatter: per level one plane through the tracked sub cell centre, side bit extends id, d = Min( d, |s| / widthDiv ). Move Shatter from CellularEdge.inl to CellShatter.inl as K6 with no change to CellularEdge's output, then call it from both.
Frame: r = u - ce, the vector from the leaf centre. Rotation by hash: 2D a small table by id bits; 3D a Householder pair; 4D a plane picked by id bits. Prototype's Rodrigues is not needed.
World: q = ( x - r + R r + drift( id ) ) * Source Scale, seed unchanged. Owner: q = R r * Source Scale + drift( id ) * 16, seed ^ mix( id, 23 ).
out = lerp( Grout, clamp( Source( q ) + lift( id ) + dot( tilt( id ), r ), -1, 1 ), smoothstep( 0, Width, d ) ). d is 0 on every wall and BSP cut, so the Source may jump there freely.
Always evaluate Source: the prototype's early return under grout is only a speed trick. Nesting is a graph: CellDomain( Source = CellDomain(...) ).
must_carry: The C0 promise covers cell boundaries only. A Source's own jump passes through: the description says so.
Width floored, or the smoothstep divides by 0 when a hybrid reaches 0.
CellularEdge bit identical after the K6 move.

nodes.range: Grout to Source's top, clamped to -1..1. No VariableRange, like TileDomain's Lookup path. Prototype -1..0.74 on marble: grout dominates contrast, as gray panels show.
nodes.continuity: C0 for continuous Source, by the mask: 0 jumps at every preset. Grout is a very steep slope, 180 to 320 per unit, which aliases at 512 px like any hard line. Step 0.00181 at 1e-5 on the default.
nodes.expected_cost: ESTIMATE, AVX2 ns 2D / 3D / 4D. Real CellularEdge Crack at 3 Levels 8.05 / 18.85 / 62.93 is the base. At 2 Levels 8-10 / 20-24 / 65-75, plus one Source. Prototype said 5.5 / 16 / 50 plus 0.5 per level, without the frame. Nesting costs both.
