algorithm: Level: at each stamp, C = Density fade * a_k( Level at the stamp's centre ), cutoff form. on = smoothstep( u, u + 0.3, C * 1.3 ), u the per stamp hash. Scale the RADIUS by on, not the height, so a stamp leaves as a smaller crater and not a ghost. The centre uses the unscaled radius, so it never leaves its cell. Level at the centre needs the inverse rotation per layer. Unconnected Level skips this.

Nesting: a separate fold, coarse to fine, additive. Lane state q[D], world scale, F, fade, amp, seed, Selected per lane each pass. A crater that owns the sample becomes the frame of the next pass: q = ( P - centre ) / radius, lattice restarted at 1 / Nest Scale. Lanes with no owner keep the current frame on a finer lattice. Rim rule: fade later passes to 0 at t = 1, inside by ( 1 - t ) / Rim and outside by ( t - 1 ) / Rim. No erase here: in a coarse to fine fold it lifts a pillar (0.46 step).

Gullies: S carried through the fine to coarse fold: S = S ( 1 - m ) + wall( t ) smoothstep( 0.22, 0.9, Rw ) radial, m the fold's own erase mask, wall( t ) smooth and zero on the floor and at the ejecta edge. M = easeOut( |S| / 0.6 ), direction S / |S|, then the stripe kernel at Gully Scale with 0.6 stripe frequency, 0.3 branching. Height += Gully Strength M stripes. Move ErosionFilter's Stripes to StripeKernel.inl as K5 with no change to ErosionFilter's output.
RimMask: the rim band of each stamp composited by the same erase rule, so a later crater erases an earlier rim.

Ink: newest layer first, one own cell per layer. Layer position rotated by the existing per layer table with fractional R2 offsets. d = |q - c|, r hashed. Transport for older layers: t = sat( ( d - r ) / ( Rt - r ) ), Rt = Reach r, e = r ( 1 - t ), eps' = 0.012 ( 1 - t ), s = sqrt( Max( d^2 - e^2, 0 ) + eps'^2 ) - eps', q' = c + ( q - c ) s / d. It is the identity at Rt, so it needs no neighbour. accum += trans a tone, trans *= 1 - a. After the loop accum += trans * Base( q ) with one read. Comb: Lu's eq 1, one direction per stage, one Floor, no hash.
Batch skips as today where a stamp contributes exactly 0: no skip for Ink's transport unless every lane is past Rt.
must_carry: Nested: outside fade (fixout=1). Without it the flagged jump comes back.
Gullies: steering field, not the analytic gradient (a slope mask on it jumps at floor and rim kinks) and not line fields (a branch cut breaks stripe feedback, 0.011 at h = 1e-5).
Graded: radius scaling, centre read.
Ink: eps softening, fractional layer offsets (growing offsets cost float precision: 923 to 583 crossings), Lu's one direction comb (the sign flip form had 5762 crossings), Rt inside the own cell.
ErosionFilter bit identical after K5.
nodes.dims: Level and Nest: 2D and 3D rendered in prototypes, one cell per level, dimension agnostic; the real node's 4D loop works, with a measured check at the port. 3D nest gives spherical caverns dimpled by smaller ones. Gullies are 2D only; 3D and 4D read Height without them, as ErosionFilter is a heightfield filter, and the member text says so. Ink 2D and 3D measured, 4D is one more coordinate, not written. GenTileable2D tiles Level and Ink through the real 4D loop; not tested.
nodes.range: Height as today, -1..1 by clamp and a measured gain per shape. Prototype nest -1 clips to 0.523: deepest floors clip on some seeds, so re-measure the gain. RimMask 0..1 then ScaleOutput. Ink -0.998..0.997 by clamp, mean about 0. Keep real VariableRange.
nodes.continuity: Crater family C0. Nest c0 6.41 straddled, step 0.00024 at 1e-5, 0 jumps after the outside fade. Graded 5.43, steep from the Level. Gullies 7.14, 0 jumps. Where two walls oppose the field cancels and gullies stop, a small blank patch and not a seam. Ink is C0 in principle and jumps in practice: 583 crossings, seam length about 6.4, worst 1.27 at default. Each is a continuous ramp over about 3e-5, passing through intermediate values, as with any crisp ink boundary. Soft 0.03 and eps 0.03 cut this to 63 crossings, worst 0.41. Comb raises it to 2256. So fnlab seams exits 1 on Ink at default, by design, and the description says so.

algorithm: Joints: per family i, normal n_i and in plane slip direction from arrays built when members are set. Loop over Families, same for all lanes. u = dot( x, n_i ) / s_i + phi, phi and s_i from the id so far (stagger: joints stop at beds and are offset between them, the biggest visual win). Uneven spacing by a monotone 1D warp: slope = 1 + 0.18 ( 2.3 cos a1 + 1.17 cos a2 ), distance divided by slope. k = Floor( u ), f = u - k, e_i = s_i Min( f, 1 - f ) / slope. Hash by per lane id, id extended by k. Last family finite: tip mask from one Perlin, below Tip the joint fades and has no offset.

Then off = sum of slips, block height = sum of lifts plus tilt dot. crack = Max over families of ( 1 - e_i / width_i )+, width decays 0.85 per family. Output Density: Source( x + off ) + height - crack depth. Warp left to an upstream DomainWarp, which is why warp members are gone: the tile note below follows from it.

Blocks: bed by 1D jittered cells on y with exact edges, 4 hashes with Selects; then row on x with per bed offset and length, then block on z. 12 hash mixes, no window, no loop. Low frequency warp of the lattice only (built in Perlin, 3 evals of 3D at fixed amplitude 0.6, frequency 0.19), S stays at p.

s = Source( p ), sc = Source( block centre ). w = sat( ( Shell - s ) / Shell ) sat( Weather ), g = 0.012 + Joint Width w. Rounded box, flat contact form: rounded rectangle in plan extruded with a small edge radius, so stacked stones keep real contact. a = Max( -d, -0.9 * 0.012 ). kept = sc > Keep + 2.2 lossNoise + 0.2 rnd, else a = gap. Polynomial smooth max with deep = s - Shell, k = 0.05, times 2, clamped.
Bed joint fixed small, so only vertical joints open with weather and stacks keep contact.

The tip mask with a joint width that narrows: 0.15 + 0.85 a. The entry's mask left a sliver.
Flat contact and Inset 0.05 on Blocks: floaters 0.82, 0.27, 0.07 percent of solid, against 1.67, 1.06, 0.37 at the rounded default. The support check made no difference and stays out.
No per block keep that depends on the lane: kept is constant in a block, and a at a face is the gap value both sides.

algorithm: Warp( seed, amp, x..., xOut... ). Frame: t = dot( x, Grain ), n across. Knots on the 3^D window of the ( t, n ) lattice, fixed jitter 0.8, reach 1.5 - 0.8 / 2 = 1.1, fade edge 1.05.

2D outside a knot, q = R / r: phi = t + dt q^2, psi = n - dn q^2, the complex potential z + R^2 / z. 3D: phi = t + dt q^3 / 2, rho' = rho sqrt( 1 - q^3 ), azimuth conserved. 4D: the 3D form with the extra axis as a second azimuth; the prototype's oblique plane ran C0.

Each term windowed by w( r ) = 1 - smoothstep( R + band, 1.05, r ) and summed. Rings inside: psi = n + K ( R - r ). Lens inside: phi = t + dt ( r / R )^2, psi = n - dn ( r / R )^2, C0 at the rim by construction.
A = Warp Amplitude / Feature Scale scales the deflection, 1 is the physical flow. Rotate the displacement back to world axes, add to xOut. Return a strength in 0..1 for DomainWarpFractal.
No masks per lane beyond inside and outside Selects. Density is a mask times weight, hashed, and cost is the worst case.
must_carry: Lens replaces the entry's Flat, whose claim fails: phi = pt + 2 dt at the rim, a jump of 2.0 on a checker. Polar has the same jump at the angle wrap.
Hold Band: entry's window median anisotropy 1.41, with band 0.7 it is 1.18.
Influence must fit the window: keep the 1.05 and 0.8 pair, do not expose them.
nodes.dims: 2D measured. 3D Stokes flow past a sphere, measured, knots are spheres and not branches, and a slice does not show a limb. 4D on an oblique plane, c0 7.92, 3^4 window. Warp output tiles only if the window hash does; add no Period. Description says GenTileable2D does not tile through it.

nodes.reuses: Thread Width (half width), Wobble, Fibre Amount, Fibre Frequency, Profile, Repeat, Output (Height, ThreadTone), A and B hybrids. Hybrid A and B give a level set warp, under which over under survives because it is topological. N, K, Step are not read.
algorithm: Triaxial: normals sum to 0, so s0 + s1 + s2 = 0; strand centres at half integers. 3 dots, 3 floors, 3 hashes for width jitter. Crossing lift, closed form: lift_a = Amp ( cos( 2 pi s_a+2 ) - cos( 2 pi s_a+1 ) ) / 2. Height = Max over families of profile + lift. Select to the hole level. Keep Thread Width ( 1 + jitter ) + Wobble below 0.5, or strands are cut at the cell edge and a seam shows: reuse Textile's existing hold.

Braid: rows along y, lanes along x. In row r crossing pairs are ( pair, pair + 1 ) with pair = r mod 2. 3 candidate lanes per sample. A strand runs straight or swings one lane in a smooth S. Over rule: right going strand over when r is even, alternating for any crossing subset. Width correction d = |x - xs| / sqrt( 1 + xs'^2 ), one sqrt per candidate or a polynomial. Height T( d ) ( B + lift sin( pi t ) ), under also dips near the over strand. At Chance 1 strand identity is integer arithmetic, so ThreadTone is per strand; below 1 per row hash.

Knot: tile ( i, j ), hash picks arcs N-E S-W, arcs N-W S-E, or a crossing. V over H when i + j is even. One hash, one tile, no window. Crossing and arc branches both compute, then Select. Height T( d ) ( B + bump lift ), bump = cos^2( pi along ), 1 at the crossing and 0 on the tile edge, so strands meet across tiles at equal height.
3D as Textile's other Structures: Triaxial a solid woven sheet repeating every 3 cells in z; Braid and Knot real tubes that rise and dive, plies repeating along z with their own hash.
must_carry: Triaxial grain: 1D value noise across the strand, not the prototype's 3 Perlins per family. Not tried in the prototype, but Textile already has Fibre Amount and it is the cheap route.
Alternating only on Braid: Random over rule shows spots where a strand goes under twice. Dropped.
Knot: bump 0 on the tile edge. That is what keeps Height C0 with no neighbour lookup.
Mask and OverUnder outputs stay out: they jump, and Textile's Output enum stays as it is.
nodes.dims: 2D measured for all. 3D measured for all: Braid and Knot real tubes, Triaxial a sheet in a slab, not impressive. 4D: pass through, as Textile's 2D pattern with extra axes reaching only the ply hash. GenTileable2D gives no cloth, the same limit as Weave: tile with Repeat. Braid: Lanes with wrap. Knot: wrap tile index. Triaxial period not implemented in any prototype, so test it.
nodes.range: -1..1 by clamp. Hole level -1, mean 0.15 Triaxial. Knot -1..0.776 over 8 seeds, so scale at the port. Reuses Textile's VariableRange.
nodes.continuity: Height C0 in all three: c0 7.95, 7.97, 8.05 straddled, step at 1e-5 0.00112, 0.00014, 0.00022. ThreadTone: per strand, jumps at a strand edge hidden by the profile; Knot tone per tile jumps by design, as today's ThreadTone text says. Sharp profile edges read steep, as Textile's own.
nodes.expected_cost: ESTIMATE, AVX2 ns 2D / 3D / 4D. Real Weave 3.31 / 4.82 / 5.10. Triaxial 4-6 / 5-7 / 6-8, Braid 4-6 / 6-8 / 6-9 (3 candidates each with a hash, a Sin and a sqrt), Knot 3-4 / 4-6 / 5-7. Prototypes said 3-4 with no grain, 7-8 with grain and wobble for Triaxial, 3-5 Braid, 2-3 Knot, and real Weave ran about 1.5x its estimate.

members.name: Source
members.note: A 2D graph. 3D Gen calls it three times, in 2D, at lane per chart seed.

members.name: Radius
members.note: Sphere radius in the Source's world units.

members.name: Sharp
members.note: Exponent on the chart weight. At 10 the cube shows on sources with large scale content.

members.name: Cut
members.note: Chart ends here, capped at 0.5.

members.name: Blend
members.note: Variance keeps std, not the range. Mean for masks. Height for hard edged sources: charts cut in over each other.

members.name: Height Bias
members.note: Height blend only.

members.name: Stride
members.note: Seed step per chart and hemisphere.

algorithm: 3D: n = p / |p|. For axis a in 0, 1, 2: ab = |n_a|, k = sqrt( 2 / ( 1 + ab ) ), u = Radius k n_a+1, v = Radius k n_a+2, area preserving. w = Max( 0, ab - Cut )^Sharp, by repeated multiply when Sharp is whole or FS::Pow. Seed per lane: seed + Stride ( 2 a + sign bit of n_a ).
Variance: sum( w val ) / sqrt( sum w^2 ). Mean: sum( w val ) / sum w.
Height: g = sat( ( ab - Cut ) / 0.12 ), gg = g^2 ( 3 - 2 g ), wn = w / ( 1 - Cut )^Sharp, best = Max over charts of gg ( val + 1 ) + Height Bias wn, wmax = Max wn, output best - Height Bias wmax - 1.
Batch skip: if no lane gives a chart weight above 0, skip that Source call. FS::AnyMask, per batch, so it cannot change a result.
2D Gen passes straight to Source. 4D Gen calls Source in 3D at ( u, v, w ), which animates a planet.
must_carry: Height's fade in g: as written in the entry, a chart with weight 0 can still win the max where its seed changes, and jumps.
Removing Height Bias wmax keeps a chart's value exact at its own centre.
Cut above 0, so a chart's weight is 0 at n_a = 0, where the hemisphere seed flips.
nodes.dims: 3D is the real form, normalising p, measured. 2D passes through. 4D runs Source in 3D with w, not measured. It cannot tile, correct for a sphere. A 2D view comes from existing DomainMap: DomainMap( Mode = Sphere, Source = SphereCharts(...) ) renders the planet to an image.
nodes.range: Follows Source. Variance is not bounded: FBm of std 0.49 reached -1.66..1.78 over 8 seeds, not clamped. Mean inside Source's range. Height biases the mean upward near chart corners, +0.35 against +0.03. Description states this.
nodes.continuity: C0 with a continuous Source: 0 real jumps on three continuous sources. The scan's default 1276 jumps come from the prototype's Dendry source, which has real seams of its own, 12 crossings on the flat sheet with no charts at all. Hard edged sources double up in blend bands. Rivers do not join across bands: they crossfade.
nodes.expected_cost: ESTIMATE, AVX2 ns. 3 x 2D Source plus about 2 ns worst case. With the batch skip on coherent grids about 1.5 to 2.5 x, most batches have one or two live charts: a guess to be measured. Position arrays can pay 3 x.

quick_members.algorithm: Probe::Jet on Guide, t = g or R90 g over sqrt( |g|^2 + e ), a fixed loop of 2 Taps + 1 Source taps with squared triangular weights. Straight takes direction once at p. left_out.reason: jet-fractal is rank 13, but its look is close to ErosionFilter and its point is the interface: see M1. An FD version ships today at about 90 ns, and FractalShaped Morse takes the slope weighting idea. cellular-multi is rank 31 and has no form without a memo: see M4.

pinnate-venation has the most striking image of the round: first on three front page lists, on four in all. It also has 3538 real jumps at default, 17x cost, and voxel and terrain give it 2. Each figure brings a long member list and composes with nothing. See M12. Flame and running-drops are close to shader recipes.

Judged from frames only. boil-pot is a staged scene, zoom-loop a Shepard zoom on plain FBm, flow-beads a still of dots. FlowNoise and hybrid seeds through SeedRoute Blend cover the plain cases. flow-beads can follow AdvectedScatter as a Time member.
Judges list these as one look. PhasorNoise, VortexPhase and Oscillator already paint it. Differences are in defect topology. turing-stencil is 73x.
Same story as SteerablePerlin and LyapunovStretch at more cost. TubeNoise Strands gives the hair case. shear-frame-ink-strokes has material 8.5, and it is the one to revisit in a StrokeField.
38x to 96x, and DendryNoise and ErosionFilter are real. Terrain reads drainage-frame's trunks as ruled lines. level-dendrite is promising for voxel only. Q5 is the cheaper river upgrade.
One composition each, unusable away from a centre. DomainInvert, DomainMap and DomainTwist surround them. domain-perspective is a camera job: the client can do it through GenPositionArray.
Open water is still missing, and these do not fill it: gerstner-sea reads as ridged land at 34x. Wakes need ships, not a lattice.
Real Stamp, StampScatter, StampLayers and FlowShingle cover these. barranco-cones reads as sea urchins at low density.
31x to 295x, and StencilFilter's modes reach most of the look. Kuwahara is a 1976 filter at 56x. A SIMD port runs a full tap set per sample with no reject.
Extensions of ExchangeFoam without a clear ability beyond its own. sign-code-regions has 17750 jumps by design. nested-foam is the one with a look, at 20x.

adaptive-cellular is rank 24: a hashed quadtree with 16 density evals, 35 ns in 2D and 1.2 us in 4D by estimate, and GradedVoronoi gives size from a map at 8 ns. cellular-density is rank 29 with 9 density evals per sample, 14 to 72 ns, and the recursion is 730 evals in 3D: SpotScatter with Coverage and StampScatter's Density cover the use. Others are below 5 or costly: peak-scatter 171x.

left_out.group: One lens terrain and voxel features
left_out.reason: slab-field is rank 28, the third of the rock group: K nearest frames repeat CellFrame at 35 ns in 3D, and beds read as tilled fields far out. bedform-strata has the same image as cross-bedding at 4x cost and 14991 jumps. aquifer-field has voxel 8.5 and a messy vol with a 27 site search. flow-watershed's basin id is a real ability two lenses flagged; it scans at 1379 jumps and 44x.

cellular-facet was wanted on CellularLookup as Slope. Left out: 5886 jumps by design, walls tear meshes, D + 1 evals. SimplexFacet and PlateDrift cover low poly. Others overlap real CellularEdge, CellularSmooth and VortexPhase, or draw a net with visible lattice at 34x.
A strange palette the creative lens enjoys, as an OrbitNoise. Relief breaks into walls, some jump (dyadic-shuffle 4736), some repeat. Nothing composes. Revisit if an art preset pack exists.

left_out.group: Coherent noises with no visible gain
left_out.reason: Technical noises that read as Perlin or as a lattice. Three are weak by their own authors' call, and ico-billow fails at cumulus. blue-lattice-noise's zero DC octaves were flagged for LOD by one judge at a score of 3.

overfold-sheet has researcher 8 and is 391x with 8762 jumps; implicit-warp gets close at 16x. vortex-pair-billows has real rolled up ink at 45x: the best motion idea, but only in motion. truchet-flow and hilbert ribbons have the lattice as their limit. glass-caustic is CausticWeb's back map. sphero-scale-fbm is a per octave axis exponent, voxel flagged it, and it could be a FractalShaped option later.
